newsitem.title: IRAQ: Three Iraqis say they spied for Israel's Mossad.
newsitem.headline: Three Iraqis say they spied for Israel's Mossad.

text.p: Iraqi television on Wednesday showed three Iraqis who confessed to spying for the Israeli intelligence service Mossad.
Jammal Majeed Nadr, 41, born in the Kurdish province of Arbil in northern Iraq, appeared on the state-run television on Wednesday evening and explained how he was recruited to spy for the Mossad.

Nadr, speaking in a relaxed manner, said he collected information about the Iraqi army in exchange for U.S. dollar payments. He said he got the information from two brothers -- one a retired army colonel and the other doing his military service at the Iraqi Defence Ministry.

Riyadh Kamal Rasheed, 46, the retired army officer, looked confused and appeared upset. He said that he wished his children and family would not know what he had done. "And if they know they should not have mercy on me."
His brother Ahsan Kamal Rasheed, 20, who was doing his military service in the Iraqi Defence Ministry, said: "There is no use for regret. It is too late."
Nadr, who like the others was wearing civilian clothes, said he travelled five times to Turkey where he met two Israeli intelligence officers.
"I travelled to Turkey five times and they gave me a radio receiver and other materials for writing secret letters," he said.
"They ask me to collect information on the Iraqi economy and the situation...and to spread rumours in order to make the Iraqi dinar slip more and more against the dollar," he said.

Nadr said he was recruited by the Israeli intelligence service through a Kurd living in Arbil, which is in the country's northern Kurdish region that is out of direct control of the Iraqi government since the 1991 Gulf War.
The Kurd told Nadr the information was going to the United Nations office in Arbil, but later during a trip to Turkey Nadr was told he had been recruited by the Mossad.
Nadr said he collected the information about the Iraqi army by recruiting the two other men, who lived in the same area as he did in Baghdad.
He said he received verbal guarantees from the Mossad that the Iraqi authorities would not be able to arrest him.

"When I was captured by the Iraqi Intelligence Department, I found out the Mossad's guarantees were nonsense as the Iraqi intelligence officers were knowing all my activities, all my travels to Turkey and even what was happening at my family," he said.
The television did not say what punishment the three faced.

At the end of the programme the presenter read an appeal by the Iraqi Intelligence Department urging Iraqis not to commit espionage. It said that if they were spying and turned themselves, in the punishment would be reduced.
Last month Iraqi television showed four Iraqis who confessed spying for the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency but Washington dismissed Baghdad's claim of having uncovered CIA spy network.
